about: Places Files treats with care. Nothing here is a wall: the console runs as t3, the same user as T3 Code's terminals, so everything t3 may change stays changeable. Managed folders are locked until 'Edit anyway'. Sign-in and key folders are open but every destructive action and every download names what is at stake. Read-only comes from the operating system, never from this list. Resolve every path below at startup from the same environment the storage manager uses (HOME, T3CODE_HOME, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME, GOMODCACHE, BUN_INSTALL), and classify a path by its real location (realpath of its parent plus its name), so a link in /workspace that points into ~/.t3 is still managed. Files never uses sudo, even when T3_ALLOW_SUDO=1 gives t3's terminals passwordless sudo.

banner.title: Managed by T3 Code and Setup
banner.body: Threads, sign-ins, backups and runtimes live here. T3 Code and the Agents and Updates pages manage them, and check what’s in use first.

children.name: userdata
openFiles: state*.sqlite (T3 Code may name it stateN.sqlite; see docker/runtime/state.mjs)

children.name: backups
children.menuFoot: Database copies kept from earlier T3 Code upgrades.
children.note: Storage shows their size but has no archive or remove action; don't promise one.

children.name: trash
children.note: Files’ own Trash for the home volume. Open it from the Trash tab, not here; deleting inside it directly is allowed after Edit anyway.

banner.title: Managed by Toolchains and Agents
banner.body: Installed agents and language runtimes. Install, update and remove them from Toolchains or Agents, which check what still uses them.

banner.title: Managed by Toolchains
banner.body: Which versions are selected and trusted. Change them from Toolchains.

managed.path: ~/.cache, ~/.npm, $GOMODCACHE, ~/.bun/install/cache and every cache location Storage detects

banner.title: Caches managed in Storage
banner.body: Storage clears these with each tool’s own command, after checking nothing is using them.

ancestors: A folder that holds a managed folder shows the managed tag of its largest managed child (so ~/.local reads “Agents and toolchains”), without the lock. Only the managed folder and what is inside it are locked.

signIns.about: Agent and CLI sign-ins. Verify each path against docker/harness/catalogue.mjs and the providers' own config overrides (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME…) before shipping; the skills service already resolves several of them.
signIns.onTrashOrDelete: Signs Codex out on this server. Paired devices keep working; Codex asks you to sign in again.
signIns.onDownload: {name} holds a sign-in. Anyone with the download can use it.

keys.onTrashOrDelete: Anything that signs in with these keys stops working until they’re back.
keys.onDownload: {name} holds keys. Anyone with the download can use them.

secretFiles.about: Single files that may hold passwords or keys, anywhere. Drawn with the file-key icon; the editor hides their values; ZIP downloads that include them say so.
secretFiles.zipWarning: {first} and {n} more may hold passwords or keys. Anyone with the ZIP can read them.

readOnly.about: From the operating system: a folder where fs.access(dir, W_OK) fails for t3. Never hard-coded.

banner.title: You can look and download here
banner.body: Changing system folders needs root, which this console doesn’t have.

noAccess.title: You can’t open {path}
noAccess.body: It belongs to {owner}. This console runs as `t3`, like agents’ terminals.
